gen-gf-medievalsharp-poppins: Bold and a little theatrical, MedievalSharp sits over Poppins, whose round, sturdy lowercase keeps its stroke weight steady throughout. And that mix of old-world swagger with a plain sans body is the strongest thing about the pair.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads dense and structured, its middle zone doing most of the work. MedievalSharp above it brings tall, crisp, commanding letters, and that jump from storybook swagger to firm slab-serif footing is the pair's real hook.
gen-gf-medievalsharp-rubik: Rubik's lowercase looks generously big beside its capitals, and its round shapes stay readable even when the type gets small. Under MedievalSharp, a long page would feel soft.
gen-gf-meera-inimai-fs-literata: Crisp, modern lines up top, bookish warmth below: Meera Inimai holds one steady stroke while Literata, a text serif, lets its curves swell slightly. Long reading would feel settled and unhurried.
gen-gf-metrophobic-fs-literata: Literata brings a bookish serif with sturdy hairlines and slightly heavier strokes, and its curves stay wide open. Metrophobic is best at flat, modern headings with that broad e, while Literata is best at carrying text.
gen-gf-mina-fs-literata: Spaghetti-like strokes, all one bold weight. Mina's spacious c leads, then Literata, a text serif with moderate contrast, offers a gentler, bookish counterweight underneath.
gen-gf-mingzat-fs-literata: Literata is bookish and sturdy, its strokes narrowing gradually toward the terminals. Mingzat is at its best as a friendly, uniform heading with a ring-like c, while Literata does its finest work with refined, slightly varied lines.
gen-gf-moderustic-fs-literata: Open gaps where Moderustic's curves end give it an approachable, uncluttered face. Its job is to greet with simple shapes, while Literata, a serif, does its best work with curves that thicken gently at the shoulders.
gen-gf-mohave-fs-literata: Mohave sets tightly packed letters with wide-mouthed c shapes and a plain, ballpoint-like line. Its pressure-free stroke against Literata's sturdy thin and slightly heavier thick lines is the sharpest thing about this pairing.
gen-gf-molengo-fs-literata: Approachable from the first line, Molengo opens every curve it draws, with hardly any stroke variation. Literata, a serif, adds only understated variation of its own, so the two feel quietly related.
